01_bm25.text: The battery is good at 3000MAH. The 1080p screen is brighter than my old Moto G6. The G7 is also unlocked and works on all four major US carriers AT&t Verizon Sprint and T-Mobile. So that means it will also work on all of their NVNO network carriers like Cricket, Metro by T-Mobile, Boost Mobile, Total wireless, Straight Talk, Google fi who uses Sprint's T-Mobile and US Cellular networks, and so many more. You name a carrier in the US and this Moto G7 will work on it. I am currently using my Moto G7 on Google fi. I can get the Sprint and T-Mobile networks in my area and the G7 switches automatically between them to find the best connection. My Moto G6 did not do that I had to force switch it. The G7 also as Wi-Fi calling. The unlocked Motorola Moto G7 is just an amazing phone.

I checked the IMEI #s on each carrier's website (they have Moto G7 listed as a compatible device) and it comes back as incompatible on every carrier I've tried (even the ones that allow you to purchase Moto G 7 on their site i.e. mint mobile). The customer service reps also checked the IMEI #s for the phone I just purchased and said that the device is not compatible with their networks. Save yourself the trouble and buy the US Unlocked version of the Moto G7 Power. Roughly the same exact phone, a few more $ and is compatible with the carriers listed in the title/descriptions. I tried Cricket wireless, Mint Mobile and also T-mobile directly for anyone curious. I hope this helps save someone the time and frustration.

Moto G7 with Alexa Does works with Metro, but you need to call them to connect.... Moto G7 with Alexa Does not work with Metro! Purchased on Amazon's Prime day and the phone did not connect with Metro's network. No matter what I tried and how many times and ways I tried to reset Moto G7 it was not working. I requested a replacement from Amazon and to my disappointment when it arrived it was identical to the first one. I called Motorola support line and their tech support informed me that this model is not compatible with Metro and I should switch to another carrier. Amazon describes G7 as "Moto G7 with Alexa Hands-Free - Unlocked - 64 GB - Ceramic Black (US Warranty) - Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile, Sprint, Boost, Cricket, & Metro"... Buyer beware this device is not going to work on Metro. After some research it seems that the version with Alexa is the one with the issue.

best budget phone for me. i love it . it's best budget phone for me ,very quick delivered too. Fingerprint reader is good , it responds quickly. For T-Mobile sim I'm not sure it will be 4G or not. now i put my country sim which join T-Mobile network and it shows 3G. In US i use note8 with T-Mobile sim (4G) and this moto g7 with my country sim for only receiving sms. If i use internet on moto g7,i will use only wifi from hotspot not from sim. For your information.

Incompatible with T-Mobile - proof included - Moto G7 Plus (International version). See the screenshot for proof. This seems to be a great phone with one HUGE problem: it is not fully compatible with US carriers (T-Mobile in particular). Some of the calls will go directly to voicemail after long silence, and there is nothing you can do. For the calls that DO get through, network type instantly changes from LTE to 3G or even "H" (which is 2G) for the duration of the call. Bottom line: this is the international version, and it cannot reliably receive phone calls in the US. Huge disappointment. I will try a Moto G7 (not Plus, US version) and see if it is any better.

Works well with TMobile, may need tech support for ATT. Even though this phone settings show its Moto g7 plus, has Moto logo at back, and shows XT1965-T inside as model number, this had Tmobile REVVLRY+ branded "firmware" from what I was told by technical support. I have used this for few months on TMobile MVNO with no issue, but when moving to ATT MVNO in June 2022, phone wouldn't make/receive calls. It could send/receive text and get mobile data, but no voice calls. This is what was found via RedPocket technical support call. Based on the SIM number it shows as TMobile branded device rather than pure-Moto g7 Plus. So ATT-side needed SIM info to change setting on carrier side, to activate voice on the network VoLTE, especially as its listed as a compatible device on ATT website with 3G being shutdown recently.

Moto G7 plus does not work well. Bought this when it first came out right from Amazon. Moved T-mobile sim card from old phone Receives calls and makes calls but only in the US The following issues were not experienced by my family who are on the same family plan as I am and also was not experienced with my sim card in other phones. The issues are specific to the Moto G7+ I bought from this seller. text messages are delayed (both sending and receiving) When out of the US no service at all on this phone

Moto g7. The Moto g7 is a decent phone with consistent performance and quality. To increase the speed go to Settings, Accessibility, Remove animations, Turn On. Warning! Be careful the Moto g7 International models are different and are not intended for the United States. International models are missing some 4G bands for the five networks (AT&T, Sprint, T-Mobile, US Cellular, and Verizon) in the United States.

The Moto G6 has a 5.7 size screen compared to the Moto G7 6.2, so the bigger the screen, the more battery will be in use. Motorola decided to give the G7 the same 3,000mAh battery capacity as the G6 and relies on the Android Pie's Adaptive Battery feature instead of increasing the Moto G7 battery capacity to atleast 3500mAh. The Moto G7 CPU is more power efficient than the Moto G6, but not enough to offset the smaller battery for it's screen size. Compared to the Moto G7 Play and Power, Motorola decided to remove Band 71 which is a great band for T-Mobile users in rural areas and is going to be a band that T-Mobile is going to use more of. It makes no sense to have Motorola's "lesser" G7 Play and Power to have this band and not the higher spec G7.

NOT compatible with AT&T, T-Mobile, or Google Fi (soon). This phone is not compatible with VoLTE on any You.S. carrier, AFAICT. This will means that voice calls will stop working when those carriers turn off their 3G networks in early 2022.
New moto g7 user. Haven't used face or finger print

I'm just grateful the old girl held on until Black Friday when I was able to snag a Moto G7 for $179 on Amazon. The transfer of Apps and Data went smoothly and both phones had the same size SIM card (nano) so that was easy. I did have to contact my service provider and update a few mobile settings for texting but that only took a few minutes and I was up and running. "Running" is the best way to describe the past two days of putting the G7 through a battery of trials and tests. First off I was amazed at the speed and fluidity of this phone, the processor is way faster than any other Moto I've owned.

My last Motorola/Lenovo phone is still going strong after 4 years, so I expect the durability I see in the this phone's built quality will mean this G7 model lasts just as well. One snag I ran into, as I needed a nano SIM card for this G7 but had a micro SIM in my old phone. I went to the Verizon store but their system rejected the G7 as incompatible or not supported and there was no way for the store to issue me a new SIM for this G7. My local big box store has a phone kiosk and they took care of getting a me a new nano SIM card. Take-away, this G7 is Verizon compatible as advertised, but Verizon stores have some issues.

Great quality phone for the price. For the price of the Moto G7, you get a rock solid phone without breaking the bank. I've been using the G7 as my every day phone for 5 months now, and I have not had one single problem with it. Don't expect the same quality display or camera you would find on a $900+ flagship, but what the moto provides is more than enough for the average user. I've used the phone on AT&T (Cricket), T-mobile, and Verizon with no issues. This phone has done so well, I'm purchasing another as a gift to someone

I loved the phone but could not get a signal when I was at home unless I went outside in the yard and I could NOT get the WiFi Calling feature to work so I returned it. Finally I bought the Moto G7 with the US warranty. It works perfectly with my Mint Mobile sim card. The Moto G7 Power has a slightly bigger screen and a much larger battery. Unfortunately the US version of the Moto G7 Power only comes in 32GB. So I sacrificed the larger battery for additional storage with Moto G7 64GB. So the moral of the story is do not buy the international version if you live in the USA!

Walmart Family mobile. We got this phone to use on the walmart family mobile network. It works great and set up was easy. Took my sim card out my old phone and popped it in the Moto g7 and it was working right away. There was no calls to coustumer service. I really love the way it the keyboard text, speaker volume works great, smooth processing and the camera is great too. Loving this phone.

Inexpensive global phone that might work on T-Mobile or AT&T. Wonderful budget phone that might work for you if you can read the description! This is a GSM global phone. In basic English this means it will work for GSM carriers like T-Mobile and AT&T IF the towers in your area have the correct bands. From a Whistle Out article (* denotes carrier's main band; phone must be compatible with at least one main band to work on network sad Carrier AT&T: 2, 4, 5, 12*, 14, 17*, 29, 30, 66 T-Mobile: 2*, 4*, 5, 12*, 66, 71* What about budget phone carriers; MVNOs (mobile virtual network operators) like Boost and Straight Talk? They might work IF you pick a service that utilizes GSM AT&T or T-Mobile and has service in your area. Straight Talk includes SIM chips for all the networks.

Best Phone on a Budget!. If you want a new phone for a reasonable price, then this is the phone for you. The Moto G7 is a great phone to buy when you want to stay unlocked and pick the carrier you want. The phone has been working excellently and I haven't had a problem with it so far. The phone can work with all GSM Carriers (ATT, T-Mobile, Metro etc.) And CDMA Carriers. You won't regret picking this up.

It was most perplexing that all my searching found no solution, only more people with the same problem with their Moto G7. I have been a Moto G phone user for years and relied on CNET reviews of the phone which was always their favorite of the budget phones. I owned a Moto G4 initially and loved it so much I upgraded to a Moto G5 when it came out. Right now I am so glad that I kept that Moto G5 because I have put the SIM card back in it and that is my lifeline while I see what will have to be one with my newer G7. The Moto G5 is making calls and working just fine. For anyone interested, I will update this review once I have dealt with Motorola Customer Support.

My plus model, not available in the US (because all the glitches have not been worked out per Motorola), used with a T-Mobile GSM SIM card, will not receive calls. There is no ringtone and no caller ID displayed. I’ve tried everything to include calling Motorola and my carrier (Ting) for help.

Moto G7 speaker issue. I owned 5 Moto G phones from G5 and up every year or so. I have always liked the value it provided. however, the G7 and G7 Plus have been disappointing in the build quality. my G7 speaker acting unstable on volume. it goes suddenly small or loud without any change to the phone. the G7 plus Speaker just broke for only 5 month of use. I would stay with Moto for a long time had the quality stayed OK.

Good phone. This is a budget phone enough for daily use. Moto G7 comes unlocked and works on AT&T, T-Mobile, and many other wireless carriers. Scree is big with a Full HD+ resolution. However, its battery is draining quickly. A higher mAh battery is preferred.

Nice Phone!!. I bought the Moto G7 as an upgrade from the Moto G4. One thing that would have been good to know before buying this phone, is that the SIM card does not fit into it. I brought my old/new phone to a T-Mobile store, and they cut the SIM card to fit. The only other option would have been to purchase a 3 in 1 SIM card for $25. This is the first day of use, which is the reason I gave it 4 stars...

Great upgrade for my old Moto G5.. This phone was just what I needed to upgrade my old phone which worked ok except for some issues with the camera. This G7 was easy to set up. I don't like that neither version of the Moto G has NFC technology because it would help to use some apps. It would have also been great to use the usb-c for video, but this also is not an option on the G7. Otherwise, the phone is great for the price (having T-Mobile, of course).

Not compatible with T-Mobile. This phone is advertised as being compatible with T-Mobile, but it is not: T-Mobile said that the phone I received is incompatible and cannot be used on their network. I purchased it directly from Amazon.

If you have Boost Mobile/Sprint BEWARE. I love the phone! What a value for the price. No complaints and I love the camera and all the features! If you have Sprint/boost Mobile though it's a huge pain to get activated. I have boost Mobile and had to go to a store to get Sprint SIM cards that all ended up not being compatible so boost Mobile has to send me a compatible sim card. If you are on Boost Mobile, there may be an issue activating your phone. I was on the phone for two days to Boost Mobile and Motorola and both have advised me that there is an issue activating the phone on the Boost network. Boost needs to have the IMEI in their system, and it took three days for the problem to be resolved. Also Boost Mobile said they would have to send me a sim card that was compatible. None of the Boost Mobile sim card kits I found had the proper card, not even their own stores So if you don't want to wait for them to send you a card, go to Best Buy and get a Sprint bring your own phone sim card kit with part number SIMOLW516TQ.

Affordable option for a TracFone compatible phone. The G7 was a replacement for an older G4 and is working fine for our needs. We aren't using facial recognition or fingerprint recognition and mostly use it for texting, calls and a little internet scrolling, so we can't comment about most features. To use with TracFone via their Verizon SIM card, you have to enter the phone's serial number to confirm that is is compatible with the Verizon network (the old G4 was not and we had service problems for three years due to poor coverage by TMobile in our area). We also have G5s in the household that we lucked out and they all worked with TracFone's Verizon SIM card, so we gambled when we bought the G7 and lucked out. Just check the TracFone site to see if the phone is compatible before opening.

Poor man's Samsung S10 - Works nearly as well at less than half the price. User experience comparable to my work Samsung S10. While the Samsung's screen is better, the nifty fingerprint sensor works only with an expensive, difficult to install, screen protector. Since the Samsung screen sticks out from the body, a screen protector is a must. Point to Moto G7 for useful fingerprint sensor. Point to Samsung for somewhat nicer screen. Samsung S10 also comes with 128 GB of memory while Moto G7 came with 64, plus expansion slot. NOTE: Moto G7 expansion slot works ONLY with SDXC 2 or UHS-II memory card. A compatible 64 GB card cost me just over $60 on Amazon. If not for the cost of the card, I would have said the Moto G7 is A THIRD the price of the Samsung. I'm not enough of a camera geek to compare cameras.
Moto g7 is good working phone. Moto g7 works great, no problems so far!

Flagship phone without the frills. Upgraded from a Moto G4 Plus to the Moto G7 Plus and I must say it is the same phone just much better. Faster charging Improved battery life Faster user interface Unlimited storage on Google pictures Better camera Great screen quality The Moto G7 Plus is a flagship phone without the frills and at an economical price.
The Right Phone. The Moto G7 phone is the right phone. Simple to use and good battery life. Easy to set up with Mint Mobile.

Good phone, Great price. I am basic phone user; texts, email, internet, social media. This phone does all of this well and as good as the much costlier Samsung i replaced. Swapped the SIM card from Samsung into the Moto g7, no problem. I will never spend $800 - $1000 on a phone again!

Great for the price!. It's been a few months and my Moto G7 has been great. I really like the interface of the Motorola smartphones. Easy to use, simple but stylish design. I upgraded from a G5 Plus. Though about switching to Samsung, but I feel like I get what I need from the G7. Compatible with apps I need for work as well.

Moto G7 has been a flawless iPhone replacement for a fraction of the cost.. Bought this phone after being an iPhone user since 2010. The Moto G7 is a fantastic phone. It took me a few weeks to overcome the learning curve required moving from iOS to android. I elected to make the move from iPhone solely because of the outrageous prices they are charging for their new line of phones. I paid around $200 for the 64 GB Moto G7 with a case and a 256GB micro SD card (a total of 320GB of storage). The phone has performed flawlessly and I’ll be moving the entire family off of iPhones and onto Moto’s over the next year.

The Moto g7 turned out to be a better phone than I had expected for the price.. There are a considerable number of questions regarding this cell phone's WIFI Calling ability. Without a phone tower anywhere nearby, this was the one 'must have' features for me. The phone's description did say that wifi calling works with the TMobile network. Consumer Cellular was very helpful and offered to switch me to a TMobile sim chip if necessary. Consumer Cellular uses either the AT&T or the Tmobile networks for their customers. CC is a reseller of those networks. Fortunately for me, wifi calling worked with the AT&T network chip that I transferred from my iPhone 7 to my new Moto g7. Now, how about the rest of the phone's features. The battery life is fantastic! Not running any battery eating background apps for extended periods, I get two days on a full charge.
Motorola Moto G7. I love this phone. The best I have ever had. I did not rate fingerprint reader because I never use it. Had zero problems using Straight Talk as a carrier on my unlocked phone.

beware of the T Mobile problem!. Motorola website says this is compatible with T-Mobile. That is true only in certain parts of the USA. It is NOT true in NY, at least for the power g7. Motorola knows it and is not doing anything about it. Don't be fooled. Don't get this phone in NY

Solid Phone for Under $300. Compared to unlocked Pixel 3a. G7 good - larger screen, Moto gestures (been using the quick access for flashlight daily for about 5 years now on Moto phones, love it) and value/price. G7 bad - battery doesn't last all day (large screen doesn't help), reception (speeds weren't great and wifi doesn't always switch over to closest AP), 1 speaker has rather low volume, and no wifi calling on Verizon (not Moto's fault as carrier decides which unlocked phones gets all their features so check carrier here as I believe ATT has wifi calling with this same phone). Overall a good phone at the price. I decided to spend the extra $100 and return for a Pixel 3A, which excels in the areas where the G7 is bad. Both are running pure Android, with a few useful extra Moto features/apps on the G7.

Great phone. This is a really nice phone and everything works flawless; updates as needed. I'm using Verizon as a carrier, and the sound is impressive. This the second Moto G7 I've owned, and would buy another if needed.
Moto g7. Works excellent

Battery life on the Moto G7 was terrible. I am an extremely light to moderate user and expect my phone battery to last at least till evening. I use my phone only for occasional calls (very infrequent), text messages (very infrequent), zero social networking except very light WhatsApp (max 4 times a day for a few minutes), web browsing and news (light to moderate), YouTube (light to moderate). The Asus last me around 2 days on a full charge. The Moto G6 Plus last me a full day. This phone - the Moto G7 lasted half a day at most ! This was totally unacceptable given my light usage. I had to carry the charger everywhere I went for the first time in my life !

Bad purchase: phone falling apart. Ordered item on Septmber 24 2021 for my mom. I have a Moto G7 which works so well so though it would work fine for my mom too but now it's acting out. The phone keep shutting off even though there's still battery life, and also the adhesive of the screen is giving up that the whole screen came off. I'm questioning if this is even an original moto g7 because the battery looks different from my original moto g7; this one has a long battery while my original one has a wide battery. I would not recommend this purchase; only purchase new from the phone carriers. I'm very disappointed with this seller.

I need this phone to replace my Nokia 3.1 Plus that was having issues charging, so I was hoping it wouldn't be necessary to send the Moto G7 to the Manufacturer and be left with no phone in the interim. My husband put the spare sim card in the sim card tray and the first one is still in the phone (under the operating one). We contacted my carrier and transferred my phone number to the spare sim card. He later read somewhere you may want to put a small piece of cardboard in the tray under your sim card prior to inserting it into the phone. Lesson learned. Other than this issue I love the phone. It's easy to use and the battery charges at lightening speed. We contacted Motorola and they said we'd have to send the phone in for repair.

Great phone for the price, a nice and easy upgrade from the Moto G6. I purchased the Moto G7 MAXX to replace my Moto G6, which after 2 years was starting to have battery issues. The G7 was actually cheaper overall than getting the G6's battery replaced. The G7 is a really nice phone. It is slightly larger than the G6 and a bit heavier, but has a much nicer, brighter screen, is faster, has a better camera, and has a much better fingerprint sensor. Other than that, it is a very similar phone, which is great. To make the transition, I connected wifi on the G7 and let it do its 3 or 4 updates to the latest version of Android 10, then swapped in the SIM and microSD cards from the G6. All of my account, app, and phone info was transferred from the G6's last cloud backup, including Tracfone minutes and data, even old SMS messages and voicemail made it over.

Awesome high-end(ish) Phone at a Low-end price!. Works great with T-Mobile, except... Native Android 9 Visual Voicemail app will not work with T-Mobile. Neither their in-house T-Mobile VVM app. My wife is stuck manually dialing into VM the old-fashioned way. According to various support forums this is because T-Mo won't support Andriod 9 yet since none of the phones that THEY sell come with it. So I guess T-Mo users are stuck until the carrier sells Android 9 phones, themselves. sad STILL - that's not the fault of the Moto G7, so don't fault the phone for a carrier issue. Other than that - it's a slick phone! All over the web this phone gets HIGH praise for its build quality, hardware specs, and capabilities at a low-end price range. It is easily a solid 5-star mid-range phone to rival Google's own Pixie, but at a low-end price of 169.99.

If you're on metro and have issues with LTE speeds and MMS sending, look up how to change the APN settings to the old metroPCS ones. They work better!

I typically charge my phone every morning, charging it to 100 percent every day. When I plug the Moto G7 into the charger in the morning, it is usually down to 82 to 85 percent, which seems a little low to me for my relatively light use. Otherwise, the Moto G7 is a nice phone for the $250 or so I paid for it. I've never had a pricey Samsung or Apple phone, but they cost $400 to $700 more than the Moto G7. The Moto G7 looks and feels good, and it works well -- I can't imagine paying 2 or 3 times the price to get just a little more functionality. It's just not worth it to me. The Motorola Moto G7 is not perfect, but it's pretty good... I recommend it.

Lot's of issues with the G7. Took the loss on this one. My old and true Moto G5 plus was the best phone that I have ever owned for the money but this newer Moto G7 was a major disappointment. My first G7 unit could not make or receive calls; got a new simm card and still no good. Exchanged that for my second G7 from Amazon and now this second unit locks up, screen and apps freeze up intermittently. Called TMobile for support and they in turn referred me to Motorola. Contacted them and Moto tech support told me to replace phone with seller. I hate this thing and probably will go back to flagship Samsungs or iPhone again. My old G5 plus after over two years still works nearly flawlessly; G7 is junk!

Very Happy! Love Motorola Phones. I switched to Tello recently and I was unable to get any mobile data working. I'm not deducting a star because they were very quick and acknowledged the issue right away after I told them I had been working with Tello's customer support for a few days without getting any results and telling them I had already flashed the phone using their Lenovo Moto Smart Assistant, which also didn't fix the issue. Phone was replaced in less than a week, they paid for everything, and now I am getting data on the new phone.

Great Phone, Just Not for Me. I love Motorola's G-series smartphones. These phones have many quality features at bargain prices compared to most other phones. I guess I've had a half-dozen or more successive G-models over the years that were retired only when Android quit updating their software. It's the same story with this Moto G7. It's a great phone with a lot of neat features, but we live in an area with marginal wireless coverage and the WiFi Calling feature on the G7 (and many other AT&T-compatible phones) isn't enabled unless you buy the phone from AT&T, instead of Amazon, Motorola, etc. For years we've depended on an AT&T MicroCell for an adequate signal, but they suddenly quit supporting them just as I was upgrading to the G7. "Just use WiFi Calling," they said. If only. So long, unlocked Moto G7. It was great while it lasted.

Overall, the Moto G7 has been a great leap in quality, speed, and features from the Galaxy S7. I think the (comparatively) minor investment on the Moto G7 will hold up over the next two years, and has already made a great impression on me.

I'm going to miss that. -No wireless charging -will try to find more

We switched phones. So now she has the G7 and she loves it. The battery lasts all day and it's fast.

All I had to do was to remove the SIM card from the G5 and put it into the G7 and I was set to go through Consumer Cellular. I can't believe the quality of this phone for the price, which is less than half, even a fourth, what the majors what for their phones. It has all the features in a phone that I want, and then some. It is a much better than the iPhone 6 that my wife has.

I have used this for few months on TMobile MVNO with no issue, but when moving to ATT MVNO in June 2022, phone wouldn't make/receive calls. Inexpensive global phone that might work on T-Mobile or AT&T. Wonderful budget phone that might work for you if you can read the description! This is a GSM global phone. From a Whistle Out article (* denotes carrier's main band; phone must be compatible with at least one main band to work on network sad Carrier AT&T: 2, 4, 5, 12*, 14, 17*, 29, 30, 66 T-Mobile: 2*, 4*, 5, 12*, 66, 71* What about budget phone carriers; MVNOs (mobile virtual network operators) like Boost and Straight Talk? They might work IF you pick a service that utilizes GSM AT&T or T-Mobile and has service in your area. Straight Talk includes SIM chips for all the networks.

Comes with a see through case that I plan to look for something a little sturdier/better looking. One negative is that the phone feels light for it's size and I would not want to drop it. Poor cell service connectivity. This "international" edition of the Moto G7 comes with a great price but limited utility in my experience using AT&T and T-Mobile service. Good phone with connectivity issues. Overall the phone is very nice and high quality, but I sometimes have missed calls due to lack of connection. Affordable option for a TracFone compatible phone. The G7 was a replacement for an older G4 and is working fine for our needs. We aren't using facial recognition or fingerprint recognition and mostly use it for texting, calls and a little internet scrolling, so we can't comment about most features. Awesome high-end(ish) Phone at a Low-end price!. Works great with T-Mobile, except... Native Android 9 Visual Voicemail app will not work with T-Mobile. Inexpensive global phone that might work on T-Mobile or AT&T. Wonderful budget phone that might work for you if you can read the description! This is a GSM global phone. In basic English this means it will work for GSM carriers like T-Mobile and AT&T IF the towers in your area have the correct bands. From a Whistle Out article (* denotes carrier's main band; phone must be compatible with at least one main band to work on network sad Carrier AT&T: 2, 4, 5, 12*, 14, 17*, 29, 30, 66 T-Mobile: 2*, 4*, 5, 12*, 66, 71* What about budget phone carriers; MVNOs (mobile virtual network operators) like Boost and Straight Talk? They might work IF you pick a service that utilizes GSM AT&T or T-Mobile and has service in your area. Straight Talk includes SIM chips for all the networks.

My last Motorola/Lenovo phone is still going strong after 4 years, so I expect the durability I see in the this phone's built quality will mean this G7 model lasts just as well. One snag I ran into, as I needed a nano SIM card for this G7 but had a micro SIM in my old phone. I went to the Verizon store but their system rejected the G7 as incompatible or not supported and there was no way for the store to issue me a new SIM for this G7. My local big box store has a phone kiosk and they took care of getting a me a new nano SIM card. Take-away, this G7 is Verizon compatible as advertised, but Verizon stores have some issues.

Not compatible with T-Mobile. This phone is advertised as being compatible with T-Mobile, but it is not: T-Mobile said that the phone I received is incompatible and cannot be used on their network. I purchased it directly from Amazon.

Not TracFone compatible. I bought this then tried to activate on TracFone (ATT) network in LA area. I gave them the IMEI number and they told me it was not compatible.

Update multiple times a day. I am a metro service network user. It works on the network. My issue is with the phone keeps telling me to restart now to update multiple times a day. I keep doing it but it keeps telling me to restart. Even after it says the update was successful. When will it end?

Another issue - the phone comes with a transparent flexible case already installed on the phone. Pretty invisible and not at all obvious. Needs to be removed in order to install the SIM card.

Outside of this hiccup, I have a better opinion of reburbished (but that wasn't explicit in the description) phones and buying through Amazon.

Not TracFone compatible. I bought this then tried to activate on TracFone (ATT) network in LA area. I gave them the IMEI number and they told me it was not compatible.
It's all good. I definitely recommend this phone if you're in the US only if you're on ATT or T-Mobile. I can't speak for the other carriers.

Update multiple times a day. I am a metro service network user. It works on the network. My issue is with the phone keeps telling me to restart now to update multiple times a day. I keep doing it but it keeps telling me to restart. Even after it says the update was successful. When will it end?

LTE/3G/2G options did not work. Upgraded from Moto G5 to G7 and when we first used it, everything seemed fine. Transfer and features accessible are good for a budget phone. Went out and lost internet access. Data did not work. Went to the settings and had to figure out APN and turn to the US setting for T-mobile for data to be accessible. I believe a notice should have been provided or set to US setting when sold in the US. As this was for my daughter, she was unaware of the issue and almost returned

Works with Verizon. I was hesitant at first after reading some reviews. "It's not compatible with Verizon" "Hands free Alexa is buggy" I use Verizon. I just inserted my old sim and have been enjoying the phone since. No problem.

Will not receive incoming calls. I’m returning this phone and getting the Moto G7. My plus model, not available in the US (because all the glitches have not been worked out per Motorola), used with a T-Mobile GSM SIM card, will not receive calls. There is no ringtone and no caller ID displayed. I’ve tried everything to include calling Motorola and my carrier (Ting) for help.

Nice phone but not working in my country for which I bought unlocked pjone.. Bought two phones for my Mother and MIL. One worked fine but this one is not working when my mom when back to her country to visit. Phone and features are nice but what is the purpose for buying an unlocked phone when you can't use it with other network sim?

NOT Compatable with Ting phone Service.. NOT Compatable with Ting phone Service even though its unlocked and works on the other carriers etc. Still going to use the phone for some other things over WiFi. Will return to rate starts accurately once it gets some time in.
Great product that is CDMA compatible. The specs are very good on this phone, so far it is working great. Works perfect with straight talk (verizon compatible SIM)

Works perfectly with MetroPCS. The phone works great with METRO PCS. I was a little hesitant but there is nothing to worry about. The phone is fully compatible with the Metro by TMobile network, including visual voicemail. This is a great upgrade from my previous Samsung Galaxy J7.

We get full 4G LTE in southern Idaho. Cons: We have had lockup issues, mostly when using the camera. There have been about 3-4 times while taking photos the phone will lock up requiring a hard reset. It doesn’t happen often and not sure what exactly is causing it other than it seems to occur the most when trying to take photos. There have also been some instances where the web browser will not display results, or simply timeout on searches when using the data plan. Normally I would attribute this to carrier problems but we both are using the same carrier and there are times when the GPS on the G7 or the web browsing will simply not work and after a hard reset will continue to work as normal.

Affordable option for a TracFone compatible phone. The G7 was a replacement for an older G4 and is working fine for our needs. We aren't using facial recognition or fingerprint recognition and mostly use it for texting, calls and a little internet scrolling, so we can't comment about most features. To use with TracFone via their Verizon SIM card, you have to enter the phone's serial number to confirm that is is compatible with the Verizon network (the old G4 was not and we had service problems for three years due to poor coverage by TMobile in our area). We also have G5s in the household that we lucked out and they all worked with TracFone's Verizon SIM card, so we gambled when we bought the G7 and lucked out. Just check the TracFone site to see if the phone is compatible before opening.

Bought 2 phones. One was not compatible with Verizon SIM. I bought 2 Alexa enabled Moto G7s during the Prime Days sale. We took both of them to a local Verizon store to get SIM cards (my old phone has the large format SIM and my wife had a flip phone) and while they had difficulties my wife's phone they did get it to work. The phone I was going to use was incompatible with a Verizon SIM. I have initiated a return/replacement with Amazon and will update this review when I get the new phone configured for Verizon. Follow up: Amazon, sent me a replacement immediately. I was able to easily get a Verizon SIM for this phone at a Verizon store. I really, really like this phone. I'm migrating from a Galaxy S5 locked to Verizon which was getting long in the tooth.

Excellent, but tricks you need to know to install SIM card.... Phone is excellent. However, there are two tricks to installing the SIM card. First - this phone can take two SIM cards, so there are two slots for the SIM cards. When I first installed the SIM card in the lower slot (closer to the bottom), phone didn't connect to my network/no bars. On line with my provider for 30 min trying to solve problem unsuccessfully. Finally tried moving the SIM card to the other slot. Suddenly the phone worked perfectly. So if you are having a problem connecting to your network, suggest that you try that. Another issue - the phone comes with a transparent flexible case already installed on the phone. Pretty invisible and not at all obvious. Needs to be removed in order to install the SIM card.

Good phone with connectivity issues. Overall the phone is very nice and high quality, but I sometimes have missed calls due to lack of connection. My phone always says that I have signal and I have wifi calling enabled for my home but sometimes I'll get voicemails for calls that never got through or i'll try to make a call and it will never start ringing despite having full signal. If I turn on and off airplane mode it fixes the connection issue. I'm not 100% sure who to blame (phone or carrier) which is why i'm still giving it 3 stars, but I never had this issue on the Moto G4 i upgraded from with Metro PCS.
Buyer beware...... Bought this phone for my 18 year old son. Says it is compatable.with Verizon. It is not. They can not get it to work on the network. Waste of money... not impressed at all.

Phone will not connect to Wifi (T-mobile). This looks like a great phone, but it will not connect to Wifi. I even received a strange text message stating "we see that your phone does not have correct settings to access the internet or send MMS.Settings will be sent to your handset" which I have never seen before and cannot find online. I did a hard factory reset, tried changing the APN settings, and nothing seems to work. I am not convinced this is compatible with T-mobile. I am very disappointed by this product and will be returning it soon. Unless I can magically get the Wifi to work...

Does NOT work with T mobile. This does NOT work with T mobile as it was advertised. The phone isn't connected to the internet at all if wifi option isn't available. I called T mobile and they told me the phone and T mobile has a compatibility issue. Why does Motorola have to lie about this? I hope they understand false marketing is illegal.

Connectivity issues, no WiFi.. Phone was good for everything except WiFi connectivity. It refused to stay connected to WiFi and was constantly searching/scanning for a new connection. Which resulted in none of the apps working. Like Alexa, Amazon shopping, etc. Constantly loading or blank screen with network error. None of my other devices had an issue so it wasn't my router. When I began researching, this is a known problem with all g7 phones, even play and power versions. Even if you turned off the scanning feature. This was under a full us warranty and Motorola costumer support was terrible. They offered to send me a used test phone as a replacement. I declined. It's a shame because it was a nice phone for all the other things.
Not all carriers supported. Doesn't work with all carriers

Also I frequently get a message the Voice for Amazon Alexa has stopped working. Since the last Android update the Chrome browser periodically locks up and you have to restart the phone for it to work again. Also the indicator showing that I have a message frequently stays on after I read the message. To make it go away I have to restart the phone. Sometimes I don't get messages, or my wife gets messages from me until hours after they are sent. I'm not sure if it's the phone or T Mobile but my wife gets them from others just fine, and the carrier says it's not a network issue. Every couple of months I have to go delete the finger prints and re-scan them for the feature to work to unlock my phone.

Did not work on sprint. Was not fully compatible with the sprint network. Initially worked with voice and data but no hotspot. After numerous support calls still couldn't get the hotspot to work and then the data basically stopped working (ridiculously low signal;nothing would load). Returned it.
Excellent. Works great with T-mobile USA. Excellent phone, very responsive, works great with T-Mobile USA. I have to yet try with a second SIM abroad, so I reserve the right to amend my comment.

My last Motorola/Lenovo phone is still going strong after 4 years, so I expect the durability I see in the this phone's built quality will mean this G7 model lasts just as well. One snag I ran into, as I needed a nano SIM card for this G7 but had a micro SIM in my old phone. I went to the Verizon store but their system rejected the G7 as incompatible or not supported and there was no way for the store to issue me a new SIM for this G7. My local big box store has a phone kiosk and they took care of getting a me a new nano SIM card. Take-away, this G7 is Verizon compatible as advertised, but Verizon stores have some issues.

I did a lot of research before settling on this model for myself and genuinely feel like it's one of the best values I could find in a phone that is compatible with my carrier. And lastly, as stated above, this is not the exact same model of phone as I've been using, so if it should happen that anything goes wrong with it or I find anything else to add I'll update this review!

Make sure it will work on your net work.. Phone worked great for about two months. Now hard to make calls, it doesn't want to connect. And when it does it's only 2G, it won't work on higher signal. I was just at T Mobile, and they told me it's out dated. Can't do anything to work on 3G or 4G. Texting works great, have not gone back to Europe yet. So can't say if it works on second sim. If your going to use it in the states, ask your carier first.

However, if your SIM card doesn't connect to your network like mine did not then you should call your service provider and they should be able to fix it and that's because some providers like MetroPCS need to activate or register your phones IMEI number in order for thr SIM card to work with your phone. What came in the box was the phone with a basic clear case on it and it has the packaging plastic cover on the screen. It did come with a USB C cable but the adapter does not work so I recommend buying a charging brick but if you already have a charging brick with a USB A port then that's fine. The international charging brick wouldn't connect to the adapter so either I just don't know how to properly plug it in or it just isn't the right adapter.
Nice Cellphone. Phone looks and feels great. Unfortunately this model does not work with my cell carrier- Republic Wireless.

Not AT&T 4G compatible. 1.5 years after I bought this I have to throw it away as it's not 4G compatible. Now, you might tell me that it is, you (and I) might believe that it is, but if AT&T doesn't believe that it is 4G then it is not. And so, they turn it off.
DON'T BUY if you're on T-Mobile or Metro by T-Mobile. Wi-fi calling doesn't work. Doesn't have support for all T-MOBILE/Metro by T-Mobile frequencies. Do not buy.
A TRAVELLER'S PHONE... Dual SIM/GSM - FUNCTIONAL Nothing Great to write home about

I need this phone to replace my Nokia 3.1 Plus that was having issues charging, so I was hoping it wouldn't be necessary to send the Moto G7 to the Manufacturer and be left with no phone in the interim. My husband put the spare sim card in the sim card tray and the first one is still in the phone (under the operating one). We contacted my carrier and transferred my phone number to the spare sim card. He later read somewhere you may want to put a small piece of cardboard in the tray under your sim card prior to inserting it into the phone. Lesson learned. Other than this issue I love the phone. It's easy to use and the battery charges at lightening speed. We contacted Motorola and they said we'd have to send the phone in for repair.

If you use Metro or TMOBILE in USA, you can't get 4GLTE. I ignored the reviews to use caution with US sales and regret it now. The seller is misleading, while the phone does work with metro, it can't get 4G LTE, leaving you with bad service most of the time. Also, the SIM card try on mines was stuck.

DON'T BUY. Couldn't get it to work on Boost Mobile or Verizon. When I called to get it activated on both they said that it was activated on their networks before but is no longer eligible to be activated.

It is not just my unit - it affects quite a number of them. The most troubling part was that Moto reps were asking people in these forums to create phone logs and send them in, but this has been going on for months. No updates or fixes and answers no longer being posted in their own forum about it. Not even, "We are working on a fix, thank you for your patience", type of thing. Meanwhile, the problem for many continues. For some tasks it's not a huge deal - you can simply switch off wifi and use LTE to do them. But things like video doorbells and some video security camera apps really do need wifi to work effectively (or, at all) - when you cannot connect to home security apps, yeah, that's a problem.

Used, no mobile data, but fixed with reset.. It's too son to give a full review. Bought the phone through Amazon Warehouse, used. Out of the box, once new SIM was installed, it was unable to connect for mobile data. after a few hours horsing around with settings, I called Amazon support who connected me with Motorola support and was instructed how to reset Wifi, data and Bluetooth... voila. A small fix like this can be very frustrating and probably causes a large number of returns. Knowledgeable support staff makes the difference, so kudos to Amazon (Brian) and Motorola (Princess). I like the functionality and ease of use of the phone, so far is very good. The lack of carrier bloat ware is nice. Outside of this hiccup, I have a better opinion of reburbished (but that wasn't explicit in the description) phones and buying through Amazon.

Troubles with T Mobile. I bought this phone for its great features and great price and paid a bit more to get it with warranty etc. It was a nightmare to get it to work with T Mobile. Calls worked but not messaging or internet, gps etc- all the data. The short answer is that Tech support (not customer service) had to walk me through changing an advanced setting called APN. It took 4 calls and 5 days and many hours to figure that out. Hope that saves others some hassle. Unfortunately I still found the internet connection unreliable after all that. Sound like a T Mobile problem, but the same sim card works fine in my old i Phone 6. Maybe I just got a bad unit, as others seem to love this phone- but it was not worth all the problems. Returning the phone.
It is a 3G not 4G LTE!. The advertisement said 4G LTE, however it is a 3G. Why selling a cell with such an absolete network?

Performance is as expected and the battery appears nearly new (per Accubattery,) unlike what some other reviewers have stated. One thing to note is that mine was still locked to T-Mobile, however there was an option to apply for an automated "permanent unlock" that succeeded (it was in the "Network & Internet" menu, under "Advanced" and this section changed after the required reboot that apparently performed the carrier unlock.) This is one of the devices, by the way, that is specifically whitelisted to work on AT&T's 4G+ network after the 3G sunset in 2022.

Problems with T-Mobile mobile data. Phone is great! But. Problems with T-Mobile mobile data. I had to work with T-mobile over two hours because the phone was not totally unlocked. For some reason the phone blocked after one week use totally T-mobile mobile data. Now its working good. But. If its happening again I have to go t-mobile shop to unlock the phone. Confusing.

Data doesn't work in Europe. Got the phone in March but just got to Europe/Hungary. No data service. My T-Mobile US SIM works unlimited data on other phone but not this one. My old Moto G4 last year had no problem. Troubleshooted all other options, it's the phone itself. Of course now it's past Amazon's 90-day support so I just wasted $300.

So, the antenna used by Motorola is pretty pitiful. Perhaps if you live in a really big city it would be okay. But if your rural by any means, forget it. Next problem. I loaded 12 apps on the G7 and half of them would not run on Wi-Fi. Which apps wouldn't run? How about Netflix, Expedia, Hotels.com, Orbitz, Capital One and Fidelity Investments. It didn't matter if you used 2.4 or 5 Ghz, same story. But if I turned off my Wi-Fi in the settings on phone, Wah lah, every app worked on the T-Mobile Cellular Data. All of these sites require a user name and password to authenticate to allow you entry. I did have 2 apps (Discover and Chase Bank) that worked on Wi-Fi. Apps such as Google translate, Weather.com worked with no problem.

Stay away from this one!!. I bought this just over a year ago. I have been fighting with bad cell service and thought it was my carrier. I changed carriers and it got worse. I constantly dropped to 3g or no internet at all. Decided to try my sim in an old phone due to some comments I saw online and I get great service. I did a factory reset reinserted my sim and still only 3g. Customer service awful. They want almost as much as a new to repair it. Wish I would have thought about bad service being the phone months ago when it was still covered. So much for motorola I'm going back to samsung.

Awesome high-end(ish) Phone at a Low-end price!. Works great with T-Mobile, except... Native Android 9 Visual Voicemail app will not work with T-Mobile. Neither their in-house T-Mobile VVM app. My wife is stuck manually dialing into VM the old-fashioned way. According to various support forums this is because T-Mo won't support Andriod 9 yet since none of the phones that THEY sell come with it. So I guess T-Mo users are stuck until the carrier sells Android 9 phones, themselves. sad STILL - that's not the fault of the Moto G7, so don't fault the phone for a carrier issue. Other than that - it's a slick phone! All over the web this phone gets HIGH praise for its build quality, hardware specs, and capabilities at a low-end price range. It is easily a solid 5-star mid-range phone to rival Google's own Pixie, but at a low-end price of 169.99.
Not Compatible with Cricket Wireless. I bought this phone for my Dad but it wasn’t compatible with Cricket.

If I can't hear it or feel it on my desk how am I going to be notified if the phone is in my pocket?! Yes, I contacted Moto tech support. Response? "Power cycle your phone"... "Wipe out and start fresh"... "Return it for a replacement"... "Verify you have a 3g SIM". Every phone mentioned above had the same issue. I've researched online - for hours. I cannot spend any more time trying to find a fix for an issue Motorola doesn't or won't acknowledge exists. Next issue is signal strength... The longer I've had this last g7, the worse signal becomes. Places I never had signal issues before now are spotty. When inside buildings sometimes the signal disappears completely. As I said, give me basic functionality. I'm wondering if that is too much to ask for... A cake of just icing gives one a tummy ache.

If ur on T-Mobile's metro PC's stay away... Good screen,decent processor but for actual cell phone use on T-Mobile metro PC's network calls drop frequently and wifi along with it's 4g service is horriffic... YouTube always has to buffer... My old phone worth less than half this price of this was x10 reliable ,I cannot even get fulls speeds or 1/3 with this phone on my router which spits out 450mbits/45mb... very dissapointing sadly it is a gift so I cannot return it.

Walmart Family mobile. We got this phone to use on the walmart family mobile network. It works great and set up was easy. Took my sim card out my old phone and popped it in the Moto g7 and it was working right away. There was no calls to coustumer service. I really love the way it the keyboard text, speaker volume works great, smooth processing and the camera is great too. Loving this phone.

Nice Phone!!. I bought the Moto G7 as an upgrade from the Moto G4. One thing that would have been good to know before buying this phone, is that the SIM card does not fit into it. I brought my old/new phone to a T-Mobile store, and they cut the SIM card to fit. The only other option would have been to purchase a 3 in 1 SIM card for $25. This is the first day of use, which is the reason I gave it 4 stars...

Poor cell service connectivity. This "international" edition of the Moto G7 comes with a great price but limited utility in my experience using AT&T and T-Mobile service. Connectivity is poor compared with the "domestic" version of the phone and WiFi calling is not available to use as a backup. The money saved is not worth it.

Works with Mint Mobile!!! Great Value!!!. Pros: Price & Value Specs are on par with more expensive phones Works with Mint Mobile Cons: Plastic body seems cheap Seems to run warm *both of these cons are remedied by adding a case. The camera isn't good as an Iphone, Samsung Galaxy, or Google Pixel but it is still pretty good. My previous phone was 6" ZTE phone from Metro PCS which I switched to Mint Mobile. I then bought the Moto G6 from Amazon and used it with my Mint Mobile sim card without issues. I felt like the Moto G6 screen was too small so I returned it and got the Moto G7 Power (international version). I loved the phone but could not get a signal when I was at home unless I went outside in the yard and I could NOT get the WiFi Calling feature to work so I returned it.
Does not support calling over Wi-Fi on AT &T. This is pretty much a deal-breaker for me as I get pretty bad coverage from AT&t in my house.
Awesome phone. It was perfect just wasn't usable on my network.

Not TMobile 4G combatible. Pros The hand gestures to activate the light or camera is cool Cons Terrible battery life Apparently not compatible with TMobile 4G network After spending some time with the device I quickly noticed it's battery died quickly and it was noticably slower at loading webpages compared to Huawei Honor 6 it replaced. After working with TMobile they claim it's the phone and not them. I doubt that but I'll try it on ATT when I can. Cameras ok Update: Apparently TMobile claims 2.7 mb is 4G speeds so I'm probably going to to switch to ATT

Don't buy for Verizon. I've had this phone since May. While it functions fine, it doesn't receive 4G through Verizon. Just LTE and sometimes 3G. Can you say Ssllooww? Verizon informed me to solve this I can just buy a new phone through them! What!? So I'm out $300 if I want 4G... It's caused me issues with the internet functionality on this phone. Timing me out, or pages not loading. Etc. Pretty annoyed.

Love My New Phone. I am a very happy customer with this phone. I sent back the first unlocked phone I tried (different brand) because I couldn't get it to work on my network. I purchased this one because it said it came with 30 days support from Amazon and it had the features I was looking for. I did not need the support even once. I use T-mobile full service (not pay as you go). Here's how I set up the phone. Put your SIM card in and then when you power up, plug it in to charge it up and leave it charging for the next few steps. Follow the instructions to connect to your wi-fi network. I have learned this is a critical step. I took my first phone to T-Mobile who really didn't understand that step.

So Verizon kindly provided me with a network extender which allows our phones to utilize our internet modem, but which requires Advanced Calling to be enabled on the phone. I hooked it up yesterday and I couldn't get it to work with my Moto G7. Problem is, the switch to enable Advanced Calling is non-existent in Amazon's version of software! Thanks a bunch Amazon. After some basic troubleshooting, I talked to Motorola support and they told me that the Amazon version of this phone is Unlocked and therefore would not support all the features that the phone carriers put in. Not content with that, I called Verizon and after an hour of trial and error with one of their level 2 tech support guys, he got it working. By the way, I can't say enough about his patience and great attitude! I now have 4 bars all over the house.

Think twice before you buy.. This phone has problems connecting to my wifi. It drops wifi for no reason. It doesn't make use of my 5g wifi connection. It only finds a 2.4g speed. It also struggles with the internet in general. I have Verizon. No reason for that.

I work off the Verizon network. For $ .99 I purchased a Verizon compatible sim card from straight talk, put it in my phone, followed the three steps they asked, and poof, I was up and running. I didn't need to talk to or contact anyone from S/T... it was that easy. Look for a BYOP kit at straighttalk.com. It even carried my remaining plan over from my old phone automatically. I am extra happy that I was able to purchase this phone on prime day, for $100 off. Thank you Amazon!

WORKS WITH VERIZON with NET 10 SIM activation kit and it's a good phone. I bought this phone and also purchased a 'Net10 Keep Your Own Phone 3-in-1 Prepaid SIM Kit' for $0.99 - That kit comes with 3 different sim cards. An ATT sim, a T-Mobile/MetroPCS sim, and a Verizon sim. Because of some of the reviews for this phone and the wording on the Net10 Verizon sim card I was unsure if it would work. But it did. All I did was put the SIM in the phone, follow the directions in the Net10 sim kit by going to their site and registering my sim, and purchasing a prepaid plan. I did the $20/month one to test. Then I rebooted the phone and 3-5 minutes later I could make/receives calls and had 4G LTE. I also purchased the Amazon recommend glass screen covers, and case. All is good.
Horrible experience. Annoying phone poor quality and the unlocked phone don't work good with my Carrier (TMobile) ended up in the garbage can

Alexa hands-free how to activate. Alexa hands-free Hard to activate keeps telling you to say Alexa but it cannot hear you. I must've said Alexa 50 or 60 times finally All 4 got excepted But hands-free for Alexa does not work well. Can be activated on boost mobile get your Sim card from Amazon Sprint Sim Kit - Your Phone. Our... Use sim card SIMOLW516TQ for boost Mobile. You can do it right over the phone after you insert the Sim. If a sprint representative gives you any problems like they can't find that Sim in the system, tell them You went on the boost mobile website and that is the SIM you were told to use. It is the correct one for boost Mobile. Make sure the number you give them for the Sim card is correct and tell them to read it back to you after You give it to them.

Not supported in the United States. It a shame, this phone should have been a slam dunk for me. It was smaller than the 7G and better specs. I did like the phone, I knew that I liked it before ordering it. A friend of mine bought one but only uses wifi calling (google) and video calling over wifi but he does not have a cell plan/carrier. I ordered the phone despite reading reviews that it was not supported with US cell service as some folks claim they did get good LTE signal (and some did not). I found a few sites that listed supported bands by phone and was very nervous that it appeared that NONE of the LTE bands could be found in the US with ATT (my carrier). Again, not sure how others were able to get LTE service, maybe those sites were wrong? I have no idea.
